model.name: Swap Variables
model.description:
How to use

Run it from the Quick Actions or Plugin menu.

Select some layers, choose source and destination variable collections and hit Swap button.


You can choose the scope for plugin: selection, current page, all pages, local styles or links in local variables (aka aliases).


After all, you may see some error. Click on them to focus viewport on problematic objects.


How it works

Swap Variables will display all local and enabled external variable collections that actually contains variables.


When you swap these collections, plugin will recursively find every used variable, then check two things:

  1. variable exists in source collection,
  2. destination collection contain variable with same group and name.


After the plugin ends its job, it will display known encountered errors below Swap button.


Known limitations

  1. If you modified external libraries, reload file to apply changes.
  2. Plugin doesn't swap styles. Use Swap Libraries instead.
  3. Plugin can't swap strokes in section. That’s not supported by Figma API yet. Do it manually instead.
  4. It may take some time to parse and swap variables when there're to many nodes or variables. Take a break and make some tea.


Problem? Idea? Kind words?

I accept feature suggestions and ideas to improve the plugin. No need to mess with hidden layers? Useful exceptions? If you have any ideas or issues, let me know in the comments.


Alternatively you can contact me via e-mail at nikita.denisov@vk.team and Telegram.


Как пользоваться

Запустите плагин из поиска или меню плагинов.

Выделите несколько слоёв, выберите изначальную коллекцию и коллекцию, которая её заменит. Нажмите кнопку Swap Variables.


Можно выбрать область работы плагина: выделенные объекты, текущая страница, все страницы, локальные стили либо алиасы в локальных переменных.


Если во время замены возникли ошибки, плагин покажет их ниже. Нажмите на ошибку, чтобы сфокусироваться на проблемном объекте.


Как работает

Swap Variables покажет все локальные и подключенные внешние библиотеки с коллекциями внутри них. Коллекции без переменных не отображаются.


Во время замены переменных, плагин будет рекурсивно искать все используемые переменные, проверяя, что:

  1. переменная лежит в изначальной коллекции,
  2. заменяющая коллекция содержит переменную с таким же именем.


Когда плагин доделает свою работу, он покажет известные ошибки под кнопкой замены.


Известные ограничения

  1. Если вы изменили внешние библиотеки, обновите файл, чтобы изменения применились.
  2. Плагин не заменяет стили. Используйте Swap Libraries.
  3. Плагин не заменяет обводки в секциях — этого нет в API. Замените вручную.
  4. Придётся подождать, если слоёв или переменных слишком много. Возьмите перерыв и заварите чая.


Сложности, идеи, отзывы?

Я принимаю запросы на фичи и идеи для улучшения. Хотите не трогать скрытые слои? Добавить полезные исключения? Если есть идеи или проблемы, напишите в комменты.


А ещё можно связаться со мной по почте nikita.denisov@vk.team или в телеграме.

model.name: Remap & Swap Variables
model.description:
Two jobs, one click: repair broken variable links, and move your color

variables to another library — matched by name.


What it does

Remap — after a library is republished, bindings in your file can point at an outdated copy of a variable. The plugin finds those and repoints them to the current one. It matches on the variable's permanent key, so it never changes which variable you use — it only repairs the link. Always safe to run.


Swap — repoints your color variables to a target library collection you pick, matched by name. Anything with no matching name is left untouched and reported.


Great for

• Multi-brand / white-label theming — build a screen once, switch it to another

brand's colors, then flip between themes with Figma's native variable modes.

• Migrating a file from one variable library to another.

• Cleaning up stale variable bindings after a library update.


How to use

1. Enable your target library in Assets → Libraries (the book icon).

2. Open the plugin.

3. Manual tab: pick Target library → Target collection, then click Remap & swap.

It runs on the current page; a progress bar shows the run and a summary reports how many were remapped / swapped / had no name match.

Frames selected? A "Remap & Swap Selected" button appears to limit the run.

Save settings remembers your target for next time.

4. Auto watch tab: turn it on and pick a target. Every new frame you add or paste is remapped + swapped automatically as you work — minimize the plugin to a small bar that shows live progress. (Auto handles new frames; run Manual once to bring existing frames up to date.)

5. Logs tab: a history of every run that changed something, stored locally.


Good to know

• Works on color variables, matched by name — both libraries need to share variable names for the swap to connect.

• No-match names are left as-is and counted, so you can handle them yourself.

• Scoped to the current page (or your selection) — it won't touch other pages.
model.tagline: Fix stale variable links and swap your color variables to another library — matched by name

LayerSweep helps you audit style usage, find detached formatting, and apply targeted swaps across large files.

LayerSweep scans selected pages in your file and groups results so you can act quickly:

Supported swap paths:

  1. Color variable → color variable

• Show how components in your design should look under different application conditions.

• Update all instances to depict a different application-wide condition in one click.

INSTRUCTIONS
===

Follow these instructions to make any component swappable using Conditioner.

1. Create a new component, or choose an existing component, and move it out of any parent frames so its frame is at the top level of the document, not embedded inside any other frames.

2. Name the component anything you'd like, but make sure it ends with " ? " followed by the name of the condition it represents. Example: "Header ? Anonymous" or "Navigation / Bottom Tabs ? Anonymous"

3. Place instances of the component into any places within your design you'd like it to appear.

4. Create a new conditional variation, also at the top level within the page. You can do this by duplicating the original component and changing overrides, or you can make a completely new frame with completely different content. Make the new instance or frame into a component, and name it to match the first conditional variation. Example: "Header ? Logged-in" or "Navigation / Bottom Tabs ? Logged-in"

5. Repeat step 4 for as many conditional variations you'd like to make for this component.

6. Wrap all the conditional variations together in one frame. Name the frame using the component name, followed by " ?" at the end. Example: "Header ?" or "Navigation / Bottom Tabs ?"

Repeat the process to set up as many conditionally-swappable components as you need. Run the Conditioner plugin whenever you want to swap all the conditional instances in your design from one variation to another.

EXAMPLE LAYER STRUCTURE
===

Setting up conditional components:
---
FRAME: Header ?
- COMPONENT: Header ? Anonymous
- COMPONENT: Header ? Logged-in

FRAME: Navigation / Bottom Tabs ?
- COMPONENT: Navigation / Bottom Tabs ? Anonymous
- COMPONENT: Navigation / Bottom Tabs ? Logged-in

Toolkit is a set of everyday design utilities in one plugin. Open it, pick a tool, get the job done.


TOOLS INCLUDED


PixelPort - Lossless Import

Bring big images and PDFs into Figma at full resolution. Figma downscales anything over 4096px on its longest edge a 2560x9529 screenshot becomes 1100x4096 and loses most of its detail. PixelPort auto-tiles the image into slices under the limit and reassembles them, so every pixel is preserved. Import PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF and PDF; multi-file; PDFs page by page at your DPI.


Font Swapper - Find, review & replace fonts

Scan a frame, page, or the whole file to see every font in use, where and how much. Replace a whole family (styles mapped automatically) or a single style, with a live preview. Catches fonts inside mixed-font layers, flags missing fonts, and locates usage across pages. Never silently substitutes a weight.


Color Swap - Find & replace colors

Scan for every solid color in use, then swap it for another color, a Figma variable, or a paint style. Locate where a color is used, spot near-duplicates and raw-vs-tokenized colors, and clean up your palette. Undoable.


Iconry - Browse & import icons

Browse the open-source icon set and import icons as reusable component sets, auto-sorted by category on a tidy library page. Restyle by size and color, bind to a variable, and drag icons straight onto your canvas.

PixelPort, Font Swapper and Color Swap process everything locally on your device. Iconry fetches icon SVGs from the public jsDelivr CDN so you can browse and import them; no design data is ever sent anywhere.

model.name: Token Wand
model.description:
You already know which design system you want. You've seen it work. But getting it into Figma with your colors, your naming, your dark mode, and accessibility that actually holds is a completely different job.


You're juggling spreadsheets. Checking contrast ratios in a browser tab. Rebuilding the whole thing when a brand color changes. And somewhere along the way, you rename something and a hundred components break.


That is the job Token Wand replaces.


✨ At a glance:

  1. Start from a real design system: start from scratch or pick a populer design system; swap in your brand colors and it's fully yours, nothing locked down
  2. Accessibility you can't break: every color in your system is calculated to meet a readability target you set; you will not get a low-contrast warning if you use the plugin right
  3. Light, dark, any mode: add as many color themes as you need; they all generate together in one click
  4. Text always reads against the right background: a button label contrasts against the button, not the page; each color role can have its own context
  5. Rename anything, break nothing: change a color name, restructure your system, reorder everything, Figma variables update in place, no broken components
  6. Dev gets the files immediately: export CSS, SCSS, Tailwind, Swift, Android, React Native, JSON and more directly from the plugin, no spreadsheet, no translation layer
  7. Zero lock-in: everything Token Wand creates are native Figma variables; remove the plugin tomorrow and your file works exactly the same



🪄 What it does


Pick your brand colors. Tell the plugin what roles you need- Background, Button, Text, Border, whatever fits your system. Choose your themes. Click Run.

Token Wand writes the entire Figma variable structure directly into your file. Every color, every theme, every variation named the way you configured, connected correctly, accessible by design. Your developer can export code-ready files the moment you're done.


When a brand color changes: update one hex value, click Run. Everything updates. Nothing breaks.



✅ Accessibility built in, not bolted on


Most tools check accessibility after the fact. Token Wand builds it in from the start.

Every color your system outputs is mathematically calculated to meet the readability level you set, not estimated, not approximately right. If you say "this text needs to be readable on this background," the plugin finds a color that guarantees it, in every theme.

A button label doesn't just need to read against the page- it needs to read against the button. Token Wand understands this. You tell each role what it sits on, and the math accounts for that. Done before a single variable is written.


You will not see a low-contrast accessibility warning. Not because the plugin ignores them- because the colors it produces cannot fail.



🏁 Start from what you already know


The built-in Theme Shop has presets for the most common design systems like- Material Design 3, Tailwind CSS, Shadcn/Radix, IBM Carbon, Shopify Polaris, Apple HIG, and more. Each one is a complete, ready-to-run setup, not just a color palette.

Load a preset, swap in your colors, run. The important difference from a community Figma library is "THIS ONE IS YOURS".

Change how many color steps you want. Rename any role. Adjust a readability target. Add a high-contrast mode for enterprise clients. Everything recalculates. No manual checks. No broken references. No locked-down structure you have to work around.


💪 Made to last


Color systems break when things change, a rename, a rebrand, a restructure. Token Wand is built around the assumption that things will change.


  1. Every color and role has a stable internal identity. Rename "Primary" to "Brand/Primary." Reorder your roles. Restructure the whole naming convention. The next time you run, Figma renames the existing variables in place. Every component that referenced them still works.
  2. For teams who want full control: the plugin also generates a structured color range per brand color (light to dark, with steps), so designers and developers share the same foundation. If you prefer token-only output without the full range, that works too, Token Wand can solve each color directly without generating a palette at all.


🧑‍💻 Dev handoff, done yesterday

What's in your Figma file is what ships in code. no design-dev gaps.


Export directly in the formats developers actually use:

CSS custom properties, SCSS, Tailwind config, DTCG JSON, Style Dictionary, Swift, Android XML, React Native, CSV audit sheet, all from within the plugin, no plugins on top of plugins.


🪄 Token Wand Made with ❤️ by me.

model.name: Prune

Prune

Prune is built to help you untangle your ever expanding design systems and files. It’s crafted to help you identify rogue or low usage elements, such as variables, styles or components, and facilitate everything from minor tweaks to sweeping updates.


Over time, files tend to collect the same kind of clutter: components no one places anymore, styles that have lost their purpose, and variables being kept alive by a single stray layer. Prune scans your file and shows you what is actually being used, what is barely hanging on, and what isn't used at all.

  2. Filterable and searchable list of elements within the selected scan type.

model.name: CanvasOps 画布智控
model.description:

根据文字描述新建设计、修改当前界面或生成新版本，支持 Web、移动端和桌面端场景。可参考当前选区的截图、层级、Auto Layout、组件、Variables 与 Styles，生成可继续编辑的 Figma 原生图层和可复用组件。生成后检查布局溢出、重叠、对比度等问题，并支持局部修正；对话与版本记录可在本机保存，方便继续迭代。

读取并批量修改外层及嵌套组件实例的 Boolean、Text、Variant 和 Instance Swap 属性，支持多选实例、公共属性及混合状态。组件内的文字优先通过已公开的文本属性更新，减少逐个进入实例修改的操作。

提供内置 SVG 图标、在线搜索和 AI 图标生成。支持调整尺寸、线宽、颜色和图标风格，并可直接拖入 Figma 画布。自定义 SVG 支持批量导入、独立创建分组、搜索、重命名、跨组移动和删除，方便整理自己的图标资源。


专业工具箱

集中完成色板生成、颜色管理、Variables、Styles 与对比度检查，让配色探索与设计资源管理衔接起来。


• 快速等距

生成等距立方体和内置等距图形，支持选区挤出、图层倾斜、厚度与颜色调整，以及按等距网格移动，快速制作具有空间感的设计元素。

将图片自动贴合到倾斜屏幕、包装表面或任意四边形，快速制作界面展示和透视效果。


• 柔和阴影

通过多层光影生成自然的外阴影与内阴影，支持颜色及光影参数调整，为卡片、按钮和展示元素增添层次感。


• Section 插入

创建原生 Figma Section，提供内置配色，并支持尺寸、圆角、填充、透明度、描边位置和虚线参数设置，让页面分区与设计整理更加高效。


• 评审标注

创建普通查看者也能看到的说明卡片、标签和跟随连线。支持说明、关注点、备注及自定义标签，可设置颜色、出现方向、连接线样式和端点图形，适用于设计评审、交互说明和交付备注。

连接两个图层，支持自动连线、随图层位置更新、添加文字说明，以及调整线条与端点样式，方便表达流程、页面关系和交互路径。

以真实字形预览可用字体，支持中英日韩等多语言示例，可以搜索、收藏字体，也能用 AI 识别字体的中文名。


安全与体验

CanvasOps 采用本地优先设计。AI 请求仅在用户主动生成时发送所需的选区内容；截图、设计结构、设计资源和历史记录提供独立隐私开关，便于控制参考范围。


使用偏好、自定义资源及选择记住的 API 配置保存在本机，API Key 也可选择仅用于当前插件会话。ChatGPT 授权凭据不会进入插件设置界面或配置备份。画布写入支持 Figma 原生撤销，让批量操作和设计探索更从容。
